1.why: A clean sans-serif face with clear label/heading hierarchy and reasonable line spacing is used throughout, though the monospace code lists and log panel are noticeably tighter than the body text.

2.why: Instruction lines such as 'Enter the delivered six-digit code.' are short, non-italic sentence case (only the brand line 'NORTHSTAR BANK' is capitalised), although the dark Logs panel is a dense monospace block on every screen.

3.why: The layout is a single narrow centred column that would likely reflow acceptably, but all 12 screenshots are 1280px desktop captures with no mobile rendering shown, so mobile readability is unverified.

4.why: Each card carries one or two plain short sentences ('Store these codes somewhere safe. Each code can be used once.'), with only mild jargon in 'Generate a secret, add it to an authenticator, then enter its current code.'

5.why: Only the recovery-code field shows an example format ('ABCDE-FGHIJ' placeholder); the email, phone, verification-code and authenticator-code fields are entirely empty with no sample input.

6.why: No step requires reading a long passage to proceed — the longest required text is two short sentences — though the persistent Logs block presents a large wall of text that must be visually skipped.

7.why: The 26-character manual secret and the eight recovery codes appear as plain selectable text with no copy button, download or 'copy all' affordance, so hand transcription is the default path.

8.why: Step 3/4 offers only 'Manual secret: zfOdAqAvBRWgTD0p-WPGgY3FkX4' — no QR code, otpauth link, or any scan alternative is rendered anywhere.

9.why: Nothing in the screenshots indicates autocomplete/one-time-code support: generic Email/Phone fields show no password-manager icons or autofill suggestions, and the OTP fields give no evidence of one-time-code hinting.

10.why: Each screen has a bold card heading and a single dark-blue primary button that stands out, but there is no step indicator or progress marker telling the user where they are in the enrolment sequence.

11.why: Most screens present one action, but the Authenticator card asks for 'Generate secret' plus 'Confirm' together and the MFA-enabled screen presents Verify, Regenerate and Log out simultaneously.

12.why: Some outcomes are stated plainly ('MFA enabled — Your authenticator is now enrolled.', 'Recovery code accepted. Remaining unused codes: 7.'), but no screen tells the user what the next step is, and the failure screen only says 'We could not complete that request.'

13.why: 'Regenerate recovery codes' and repeated 'Generate secret' allow retrying without penalty, and codes remain visible, but there is no reveal/hide toggle and no way to re-display previously issued codes once dismissed.

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request.', avoids blaming the user but names neither the actual problem nor any corrective step, so the statement as a whole does not hold.

15.why: Reading is untimed, but the authenticator step imposes an explicit expiry ('Current test code: 130841 (expires at 19:55:30)'), so code entry is time-limited rather than generous.
